evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52 h = 9.92 mg/L (minimum constraint 2.0 mg/L; large margin)
Receiving P assays: 0.022 g/L @24h, 1.074 @36h, 2.943 @48h — monotonic, healthy ramp
Source batches 1-3 P at same time points: ~0-0.03, 1.02-1.12, 2.98-3.06 g/L; peaks ~8.1-8.4 g/L at 72-84h
Receiving DO2 dip to ~7.4-8.4 mg/L at 24-28 h matches source pattern and recovers fully
No evidence of overfeeding or oxygen limitation that would justify feed reduction or aeration increase
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation matches the healthy source-batch ensemble at every observable point: P at 36 h (1.074 g/L) and 48 h (2.943 g/L) fall inside the source range, and DO2 (9.9 mg/L at 52 h) is far above the 2.0 mg/L minimum with the same transient dip-and-recovery pattern seen in all three sources. Feed reduction or a stop would sacrifice product mass during the 52-84 h window where sources gain ~5 g/L; increasing air adds nothing when DO is already non-limiting. KEEP preserves the projected trajectory toward the ~8 g/L source-class peak.
submission.uncertainty: Receiving hidden parameters may differ from sources; only delayed P assays through 48 h are available (next assay at 56 h would confirm the ~5.4-5.5 g/L region). Source trajectories decline slightly after 72-84 h, so optimal harvest timing matters but is outside the intervention menu. Confidence in KEEP is high since no observable deviates from the healthy ensemble.
